contentBlocks.text: SASSA Older Person Grant Eligibility Guide

When you reach the age of 60, you transition from unemployment support (SRD) to the state pension — the Older Person Grant. This grant provides R2,400 per month (R2,420 for those 75+) and is the most substantial social grant in South Africa.

The Older Person Grant fulfils the constitutional right to social security for elderly South Africans. Unlike the SRD R370 grant (which stops at 60), the Older Person Grant is a permanent, monthly income for those aged 60 and above who meet the means test requirements. It increases annually with the national budget.

Mpho is a 63-year-old retired teacher from Limpopo. She receives a small government pension of R3,000 per month from GEPF. Her total annual income is R36,000, well below the R112,200 single threshold. Mpho qualifies for the Older Person Grant despite receiving a pension. She also explored the Grant-in-Aid for her husband who requires full-time care. This guide explains exactly what Mpho — and anyone approaching 60 — needs to know.
Which Grants You Can Apply For

rows: Means test: income below R112,200/yr (single) or R224,400/yr (married)
Requires medical proof of need for 24-hour care

checklist: Must be a South African citizen, permanent resident, or refugee
Must not live in a state-funded institution (e.g., state old age home)
Must not receive another social grant for yourself
Annual income must be below R112,200 (Single) or R224,400 (Married)
Total assets must be below R1,584,000 (Single) or R3,168,000 (Married)
restrictions: You cannot receive the SRD R370 grant once you turn 60 — you must migrate to the Older Person Grant
If you live in a state-funded institution, you do not qualify
Assets include property (excluding your primary home), investments, and cash savings

documents.label: Original 13-digit barcoded Smart Card ID or green ID book
Proof of marital status (marriage certificate, divorce order, or spouse's death certificate)
Proof of residence (utility bill or letter from local chief/traditional authority)
Proof of income and assets (last 3 months bank statements, pension slips)
If unemployed, an affidavit confirming unemployment sworn at SAPS

steps.title: Gather your documents
steps.description: Collect your green ID book or smart card, proof of marital status, proof of residence, and income/asset statements.

steps.title: Find your nearest SASSA office
steps.description: Visit your local SASSA office. You can find addresses and operating hours on our office finder page.

steps.title: Complete the application form
steps.description: Fill in the Older Person Grant application form with the assistance of a SASSA officer.

steps.title: Undergo verification
steps.description: SASSA will take your fingerprints, verify your identity with Home Affairs, and assess your means test documents.

steps.title: Wait for processing
steps.description: Applications take up to 3 months to process. Payments are backdated to the application date if approved.

contentBlocks.title: Processing Timeline
contentBlocks.text: Processing time: up to 3 months. If approved, payments are backdated to your application date. You should apply as soon as you turn 60 or as soon as your income drops below the threshold.

items: Waiting too long to apply after turning 60 — you lose potential backpay if you delay
Not declaring all assets — SASSA cross-checks with banks and property registries
Assuming a private pension fully disqualifies you — many pensioners still qualify if their income is below the threshold
Not applying for Grant-in-Aid if you need full-time care — this is a separate application process

contentBlocks.text: What to Do If Your Application Is Declined

If your Older Person Grant is declined, you have 90 days from receiving the decline notification to appeal. Common reasons for decline include exceeding the means test threshold, failing identity verification, or SASSA finding you are registered for another grant. Visit our appeals centre for step-by-step guidance.

faqs.question: When does the pension increase to R2,420?
faqs.answer: Beneficiaries aged 75 and older automatically receive an extra R20 per month, bringing their total pension to R2,420. This increase does not require a separate application.

faqs.question: Can I receive the SRD R370 grant after I turn 60?
faqs.answer: No. Once you turn 60, you must transition to the Older Person Grant. The SRD R370 is only for adults aged 18-59. You cannot receive both.

faqs.question: Can I get the Older Person Grant if I still work part-time?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided your total annual income from all sources (including part-time work) falls below R112,200 for a single person or R224,400 for a married person.

faqs.question: What happens if my spouse passes away?
faqs.answer: Your means test threshold changes from the married limit to the single limit. Your grant amount is not affected, but you must update your marital status with SASSA.

faqs.question: Can I apply for the Older Person Grant online?
faqs.answer: No. The Older Person Grant requires an in-person visit to a SASSA office with original documents. Only the SRD R370 grant can be applied for online.

faqs.question: Will my grant increase automatically every year?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Minister of Finance announces annual grant adjustments during the February budget speech. Increases typically take effect from April and October.

faqs.question: Can I apply for Grant-in-Aid at the same time?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you need a separate medical assessment and application form for Grant-in-Aid. It is not automatically included with the Older Person Grant.
